findings.what: AC2's ONE new deep destination is built from the wrong id. `needsYouRowHref` returns `workDetailHref(row.client_id, row.task_id)` for a `work_question` row, but `list_review_queue`'s `work_question_rows` publishes `task_id` = `agent_interruptions.task_id` (an `agent_tasks` id), while the accounting Work is a DIFFERENT column, `agent_interruptions.work_id`. The link therefore addresses `/clients/:clientId/work/<agent_task_id>` — a Work-detail route that resolves nothing.
findings.evidence: MEASURED off live `pg_proc` on clara_659: `clara.list_review_queue`'s body contains `wqi.id question_id,wqi.task_id,...` in the same select whose Work join is `join clara.accounting_work wqw on wqw.id=wqi.work_id` (prosrc read this pass; the file text is packages/db/migrations/0180_work_questions.sql:1069-1078). `clara.open_work_question` inserts `(task_id, ..., work_id, ...) values (p_task, ..., w.id, ...)` — two different ids (0180_work_questions.sql:665-670). MEASURED column list of clara.agent_interruptions carries BOTH `task_id` and `work_id`. The consumer side: apps/web/lib/journals/types.ts:152-155 documents this field as "keyed by TASK id (each pending interruption's OWN `task_id`, never the interruption's own id), resolved via `clara.agent_tasks_visible`"; apps/web/app/(firm)/clients/[clientId]/work/[workId]/page.tsx:29-36 passes the path segment straight to `WorkDetail` as `workId`, which reaches `loadWorkDetail` -> `getAccountingWork(clientId, workId)` (apps/web/lib/work/reads.ts:190-193) and returns null for an id that is not an `accounting_work.id` — and that same loader reads the Work's own task separately as `work.current_task_id` (reads.ts:201), which is the id the queue row actually carries. The unit cell cannot catch this: apps/web/lib/firm/needs-you-links.test.ts:51-58 asserts the builder's output string against a made-up uuid (`33333333-...`), so it is true by construction; no db or browser cell follows a real `work_question` row to the Work page.
findings.fix: The Work id is not on the row today. Either (a) leave `work_question` on its pre-#659 fall-through to `/clients/<id>` and name the missing `work_id` column as a residual against 0180's queue row, or (b) add `work_id` to the `work_question_rows` CTE in a new migration and link off THAT, never off `task_id`. Whichever is chosen, the cell must be a real row (a db battery that opens a work question and asserts `row.task_id <> work.id`), not a synthetic uuid.

findings.what: The `recent_success` count and the link it opens are different populations. The pack counts a client's Work by COMMITTED RECEIPT date (`operation_receipts.created_at` inside the seven-day MYT window); the drilldown opens `/work?client=<id>&status=completed&since=<from>&until=<to>`, and `clara.list_accounting_work` applies that window to `w.created_at` — when the Work STARTED. The module's own comment at :299-301 claims the opposite ("so a drilldown cannot mean a different week"), and the surface's disclosure sentence only describes the COUNT's basis, never the LINK's.
findings.evidence: MEASURED on clara_659 off live prosrc. Pack: `), recent as ( select o.client_id, count(distinct o.work_id) ... where o.outcome = 'committed' and o.created_at >= v_from and o.created_at < v_to` (packages/db/migrations/0231_firm_portfolio_pack.sql:478-486). List door: `and (p_since is null or w.created_at >= p_since) and (p_until is null or w.created_at < p_until)` (0203_list_accounting_work_intent_key.sql:340-341). The href builder passes the pack's own window dates unchanged (portfolio-pack.ts:323-329) and apps/web/lib/work/work-list.ts:117-118 converts them to that instant range. Failure scenario: a Work created 30 days ago and posted 2 days ago is counted (recent_success = 1) and is NOT in the list the count links to -> the professional clicks "1" and lands on an empty Work list. The reverse case exists too (a Work created inside the window, status `completed`, with no committed receipt — the door's own `uncounted_completions` case — is in the list and not in the count). The e2e leg does not measure this: apps/web/e2e/home-board-walk.spec.ts:675-677 asserts only the URL shape and a mock-supplied row.
findings.fix: Either drop `since`/`until` from the recent_success href (open `?client=<id>&status=completed` and say on the surface that the list is not narrowed to the week), or state the divergence in `FirmHome.portfolio.recentDatedBy` in the shape D18.e asked for — the count is receipt-dated, the list it opens is start-dated, #905 owns the receipt-dated window. Then correct portfolio-pack.ts:299-301, which currently asserts the divergence away.

findings.what: `p659.home.drilldown` claims "focus returns to the control that left it" and cannot measure it. The poll asserts `document.activeElement?.textContent` `.toContain("3")` — a HARD-CODED literal inside a three-leg loop, where the sibling #650 cell at :504-506 correctly asserts `.toContain(name)`, the loop variable. Each portfolio count link renders only its number as text (`<Link ... aria-label={...}>{n}</Link>`, firm-portfolio-section.tsx:173-180), so the three legs' focused nodes would read "3", "2" and "1".
findings.evidence: MEASURED: `pnpm --filter @clara/web e2e home-board` -> 15 passed. If focus were restored to the clicked link, leg 2 (`"2 Work needing attention for Rome Properties"`) would yield textContent "2" and `.toContain("3")` would FAIL. The suite is green, so `document.activeElement` is NOT that link on legs 2 and 3 — the poll is reading an ancestor/`<body>` whose textContent contains "3" (the board also renders "Needs you: 3"). The assertion therefore passes identically with focus restoration entirely absent, and nothing in firm-portfolio-section.tsx or use-firm-portfolio.ts restores focus after a `goBack`. AC7's "keyboard/focus return" and AC2's second half are green on an assertion that cannot fail.
findings.fix: Use the loop variable (`.toContain(name)` is still weak on a `<body>` read — prefer `page.evaluate(() => document.activeElement?.getAttribute('aria-label'))` and compare to `name`). If that reds, the focus-return obligation is unmet and belongs in the report as a gap, not as a green cell.

findings.what: The filtered-empty state makes a FIRM-WIDE claim out of a PAGE-LOCAL filter. `visiblePortfolioRows` narrows only `pack.rows` — the current keyset page of at most 50 clients (the door takes no filter argument, portfolio-url-state.ts:29-31) — but the Empty renders `FirmHome.portfolio.emptyFilteredBody`: "The firm has clients — none of them matches the narrowing in the address bar." On a firm with more than one page, a client that exists and matches is simply on a later page.
findings.evidence: MEASURED with a throwaway cell mounted on the real component (deleted after the run): with `?q=zeta` and a pack whose `truncated` is true and `nextCursor` is set, the rendered text was "... No client matches this viewThe firm has clients — none of them matches the narrowing in the address bar.Clear th..." while the Next-page control was present on the same screen. Code path: firm-portfolio-section.tsx:158 (`visiblePortfolioRows(pack.rows, ...)`), :246 (`if (rows.length === 0 && filtered)`), :251 (`emptyFilteredBody`), messages/en.json `FirmHome.portfolio.emptyFilteredBody`. Failure scenario: a 60-client firm, `?status=archived`, the single archived client is row 55 -> the board tells a principal no client in the firm is archived.
findings.fix: Reword the sentence to the truth the build can support ("No client on this page matches …" plus the page number/Next hint), or push `status`/`q` into the door as real arguments and keep the firm-wide claim. The same page-local caveat applies to `?attention=needs_you`, which is derived from the review queue's own paged `rows` (firm-home-board.tsx:112-115).

findings.what: `?? 0` turns "this build could not read the count" into "every client is clear" — the exact bug portfolio-pack.ts:11-13 and :5-9 forbid by name ("UNKNOWN IS NOT ZERO", "the same `?? 0` anywhere in this file would be the same bug"). `caughtUp` is computed as `pack.rows.every((r) => (r.active ?? 0) === 0 && (r.attentionFailed ?? 0) === 0)`, and `rowMatchesAttention`'s `caught_up`/`active`/`failed` arms do the same.
findings.evidence: MEASURED with a throwaway cell on the real component (deleted after the run): mounting `FirmPortfolioSection` with a single row whose `active`, `attentionFailed` and `recentSuccess` are all null rendered BOTH "could not be read" AND "Every client is clear: nothing is running and nothing needs attention" on one screen. A second cell measured `visiblePortfolioRows([unknownRow], {attention:'caught_up'}, new Set())` -> length 1: the `caught_up` narrowing KEEPS a client whose counts are unknown, and the `active`/`failed` narrowings drop it. The existing cell firm-portfolio.test.tsx:129-135 proves only the count CELL prints "could not be read"; nothing asserts the caught-up sentence is withheld.
findings.fix: Make `caughtUp` require a known zero (`r.active === 0 && r.attentionFailed === 0`) so a null suppresses the reassurance, and give `rowMatchesAttention` an explicit null arm. Add a cell that asserts "Every client is clear" is ABSENT when any count is null.

findings.what: The row's single `coverage_reason` is a strict precedence, so a client that is BOTH onboarding/archived AND carries undated completions publishes only `onboarding_client_excluded_from_queue`. The browser renders exactly one coverage sentence off that token (firm-portfolio-section.tsx:188-199), so the `recent_success = 0` beside an undated completion is shown with no explanation at all — and the brief's rule ("every row whose labels were cut carries coverage='partial' with coverage_reason='retry_label_preview_only'") is likewise silently lost whenever an earlier arm wins.
findings.evidence: MEASURED on clara_659 with a throwaway battery cell (deleted after the run): one archived client, one Work admitted, claimed and settled `completed` with no receipt. The pack returned `{"status":"archived", ... "recent_success":0, "coverage_reason":"onboarding_client_excluded_from_queue", "uncounted_completions":1}` — the row really does carry an undated completion and the row's only published reason is the status one. `uncounted_completions` is on the row but the surface never reads it except as the count argument of the `completions_without_receipt` message it is not rendering (firm-portfolio-section.tsx:192).
findings.fix: Either publish `coverage_reasons` as an ARRAY (all applicable tokens) and render each, or keep the single token and render the `completions_without_receipt` sentence off `uncountedCompletions > 0` independently of `coverageReason`. State the chosen rule in the migration header, which today describes the precedence as if only one condition could apply at a time.

findings.what: AC6 asks for an ATTRIBUTABLE actor on the disposition receipt; the receipt prints the raw user uuid. `clara.compliance_watch_events.actor` is `text` holding `c.actor::text` (a user id), and the card renders it straight into "Acknowledged by {actor} on {at}". The same lane, in the same commit, resolves an actor uuid to a display name for the activity band through `ActivityActorLine` (firm-recent-activity.tsx:35).
findings.evidence: packages/db/migrations/0016_a21_compliance_watch.sql:359-370 types `actor text`; :1081-1091 stamps `acknowledged_by=c.actor::text` and inserts the event with `c.actor::text`. The receipt's own cell PINS the uuid as correct: apps/web/components/firm/compliance-watch-receipt.test.tsx:98 fixtures `actor: "8a7b6c5d-0000-4000-8000-000000000001"` and :158-159 asserts `/Acknowledged by 8a7b6c5d-0000-4000-8000-000000000001/` with the comment "the actor is the one the DATABASE stamped, never the reader". A professional reading the card sees a uuid, not a colleague.
findings.fix: Resolve the actor through the same `firm_members_visible` roster the activity band already uses (or reuse `ActivityActorLine`), falling back to the uuid only when the roster does not answer, and repoint the cell at the resolved name.

findings.what: The extracted module's header asserts a fact that is false in the same commit: "`add-client-control.test.tsx` and `add-client-candidates.test.tsx` are repointed at this module in the same commit and assert exactly what they asserted before." Neither file was repointed; both still mount `ClientRegisterList`. The brief required the repoint ("both import from the old location and must be repointed in the same commit") and the worker's own report records the opposite as Assumption (2).
findings.evidence: apps/web/components/firm/add-client-control.test.tsx:34 `import { ClientRegisterList } from "./client-register-list";` and apps/web/components/firm/add-client-candidates.test.tsx:26 the same. Consequence: the extracted module has no direct unit cell — it is exercised only transitively, and its NEW property (mounting beside a state machine on a page with four re-read triggers) is proven only by the browser leg. Precedent this violates: app/(firm)/page.tsx:8-13's own rule that a stale claim in source is the same class of lie as a premature one.
findings.fix: Either repoint both cells at `./add-client-control` (the brief's instruction) or delete the sentence and say plainly that the two cells stay on `ClientRegisterList` as #649's AC1 evidence at its own surface — which is the defensible choice, but it has to be what the file says.

findings.what: The cell titled "... p_preview=0 calls the helper zero times" never measures a call. It asserts only that each row's `preview` is `[]` and its `active` count is unaffected. The body in fact keeps `left join clara._work_run_attempts(v_labelled)` in the statement unconditionally with `v_labelled = '{}'`, so whether the helper executes is a PLANNER decision, not a guaranteed zero — and the migration contradicts itself about it: the header says "`p_preview = 0` calls the helper NOT AT ALL — the cheap page" (0231:118-120) while the body comment 40 lines later says "p_preview = 0 reaches it with no ids rather than with a null" (0231:495-497).
findings.evidence: packages/db/migrations/0231_firm_portfolio_pack.sql:498 `left join clara._work_run_attempts(v_labelled) a on a.work_id = w.id`; :496 the body comment; :118-120 the header claim; the closing tail NOTICE repeats "cuts the preview array at 101 before clara._work_run_attempts is asked anything". The helper itself tolerates an empty array (0189_work_list_reads.sql:269-272 refuses only a NULL array or >101 ids), so nothing is broken — the defect is a title and a header that assert a measurement the file never made.
findings.fix: Either guard the join (`case when v_preview > 0 then ...`, or skip pass 3's preview CTE entirely) and then measure the zero calls with `pg_stat_user_functions` / a session counter, or rewrite the cell title and the header to the truth: the helper is asked with an EMPTY array, which it admits.

findings.what: A superseded read clears the busy flags unconditionally, so a stale response can hand the board a `loading: false` + empty pack frame that renders the first-use "No clients yet" Empty while the current read is still in flight. The epoch guard protects the DATA but not `loading`.
findings.evidence: use-firm-portfolio.ts:146 `if (epoch !== epochRef.current) return;` on the success path and :157 on the error path, then :165-167 `setLoading(false); setRefreshing(false);` in `finally` with the comment "UNCONDITIONAL". The page-change effect at :175-186 sets `pack = EMPTY_PORTFOLIO_PACK` and `loading = true` before issuing the read, and `hasLoadedOnceRef` is reset to false, so a second trigger (focus, the 30 s tick, CLIENT_RECORD_CHANGED) that fires during a slow page turn produces epoch N+1; when the slower epoch N settles it returns early and then clears `loading`. firm-portfolio-section.tsx:238-245 then renders `pack.rows.length === 0` -> `portfolio.emptyRegisterTitle` ("No clients yet"). Failure scenario: click Next on a large register, alt-tab back while it loads -> the board briefly says the firm has no clients.
findings.fix: Gate the `finally` on the epoch (`if (epoch === epochRef.current) { setLoading(false); setRefreshing(false); }`), or keep `loading` true while `epochRef.current` names an outstanding read. A cell that starts two reads and settles them out of order would hold it.

findings.what: D18.f's swap leaves `lib/firm/timeline.ts` — and with it `clara.list_firm_timeline` (0174) — with no production consumer, while `lib/firm/timeline.test.ts` stays in the run manifest and keeps testing it. The deleted `firm-timeline-section.tsx` was its only caller.
findings.evidence: `grep -rn "firm/timeline"` over apps/web returns only `lib/firm/timeline.test.ts:16` (the import under test) and two prose references in `lib/firm/activity.ts:31` and `lib/work/evidence.ts:129`. apps/web/test/manifest.txt:320 still lists `lib/firm/timeline.test.ts`. The worker's report names five follow-ups and this is not among them.

findings.what: #659 added a `get_firm_portfolio_pack` handler but NO `list_activity` handler, and the home board now reads `list_activity`. `serve-built.mjs` dispatches `handleActivitySupabase` at :609, far above `handleHomeBoardSupabase` at :720, so every OTHER lane's walk that merely lands on `/` now renders #632's activity fixtures in Firm Home's recent-activity band. The worker disclosed this in its report as a "coverage change, named"; the ownership census cannot see it because this lane declares no handler for the verb.
findings.evidence: apps/web/e2e/serve-built.mjs:609 vs :720 (measured this pass). apps/web/e2e/home-board-walk.spec.ts:254-258 states the same fact and overlays its own `page.route` for this lane only. The `e2e-fixture-ownership.test.ts` declaration added at :361-372 covers `get_firm_portfolio_pack` (unscopeable) and says nothing about `list_activity`.
findings.fix: Either answer `list_activity` from `home-board-mock.mjs` with an honest empty envelope (dispatch position unchanged — the new arm sits beside `get_firm_portfolio_pack`, above `EMPTY_RPCS`, which §6.1 permits since it is not the EMPTY_RPCS arm), or record the shared dependency in `SHARED_RPC_VERBS`/the lane declaration so the census owns it rather than a report paragraph.

findings.what: The empty-name cursor fence would refuse a cursor the door itself minted, if a client's name were blank: the mint is `lower(name)||'|'||id` (0231:556-558) and the decode raises `invalid_cursor` when `btrim(name)` is empty. That would dead-end paging at that client. NOT reachable today, which is why this is a note and not a finding.
findings.evidence: MEASURED on clara_659 (throwaway cell, deleted after the run): `clara.create_client(p_name => '   ')` refuses CLR10 'client name and op_key are required'; a forged whitespace-name cursor is refused CLR10 'malformed portfolio cursor'; and `grep` over packages/db/migrations for a client-rename door found none, so `clara.clients.name` cannot become blank after birth through any door. The row only exists if someone writes it with owner DML.
findings.fix: Nothing to change. Worth one sentence in the migration header so a later lane that adds a rename door knows the cursor grammar depends on a non-blank name.
